title: Methodus nova et facilis calculum variationum tractandi

deep.reconstruction:
Context: E420 ('Methodus nova et facilis calculum variationum tractandi', Novi Comm. Petrop. 16, 1771/72). Here Euler recasts variational calculus as ordinary differentiation in an auxiliary parameter t. The varied surface is z = z(x,y,t), and the variation of any quantity W is dt·(∂W/∂t). On the previous page he introduced double integrals ∫∫V dx dy over a fixed base region in the horizontal plane, for surface problems. He noted that the order of the two integrations is immaterial and referred to his own E391 in Tom. XIV.

§25. Because the base region and the variables x, y are not varied, the variation of J = ∫∫V dx dy is δJ = dt ∫∫(∂V/∂t) dx dy. This is again a double integral. It can be written as an iterated integral in either order: dt∫dx∫(∂V/∂t)dy or dt∫dy∫(∂V/∂t)dx.

§26. Take V as in §19: a function of x, y, z and the partial derivatives of z up to some order, with coefficients N, P, P', Q, Q', Q'', R, R', R'', R''' (the partial derivatives of V with respect to z, z_x, z_y, z_xx, z_xy, z_yy, z_xxx, ...). Then by §23,
∂V/∂t = N z_t + P z_xt + P' z_yt + Q z_xxt + Q' z_xyt + Q'' z_yyt + R z_xxxt + R' z_xxyt + R'' z_xyyt + R''' z_yyyt + ...
Substituting gives the first variation as a sum of double integrals, each a coefficient times a mixed t-derivative of z. That is the modern δJ = ∫∫ Σ_α (∂V/∂(∂^α z)) ∂^α(δz) dx dy with δz = dt·z_t.

Purpose: prepare for §27 onward. There each term after the first is integrated by parts in x or y, moving derivatives off z_t. The result is the Euler–Lagrange (Euler–Ostrogradsky) equation N − ∂_xP − ∂_yP' + ∂_xxQ + ∂_xyQ' + ∂_yyQ'' − ... = 0, plus single-integral boundary terms.
errors: No mathematical error on this page.

The expansion of ∂V/∂t is valid only for V 'of the first genus' (a pure function of x, y, z and derivatives of z), although §25 mentions V of either the first or second genus. Second-genus V, containing integral formulas, needs extra terms; these are not handled here.

Gap (inherited from the framework): the base region is tacitly fixed, and its boundary is unspecified. The boundary terms that appear in §27 (∫P z_t dy, etc.) are treated loosely for a non-rectangular domain. This is a known limitation of Euler's (and Lagrange's) early treatments of multiple-integral variations.

ideas.what: First variation of a double integral obtained by differentiating under the integral sign with respect to an embedding parameter t (δ = dt ∂/∂t), with a fixed domain.
ideas.modern_name: First variation via one-parameter family (Gateaux derivative) for multiple integrals
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lagrange (1760–61, δ-method for double integrals, minimal surfaces); Euler E420 for the parameter-t formulation
ideas.where_published: E420 itself; also Institutionum calculi integralis vol. III appendix (E385) for the t-method in the single-integral case

ideas.what: Equivalence of the two iterated integration orders for the double integral of the variation.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler E391 (De formulis integralibus duplicatis) for systematic treatment; Fubini 1907 rigorous

ideas.what: Expansion of ∂V/∂t through the chain rule into coefficient-weighted mixed partials z_{x^i y^j t}, up to third-order derivatives of z.
ideas.modern_name: Linearization of a higher-order Lagrangian; jet-space chain rule

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine setup step: the variation of a double integral written as a sum of terms awaiting integration by parts. E420 and its double-integral Euler–Lagrange derivation are well documented in the Opera omnia (series I vol. 25) and in histories of the calculus of variations (e.g. Goldstine, Fraser).
transcription_corrections: The transcription matches the image essentially exactly. The printed 'dx. dy' in the second term is a typographical period in the original, not a mathematical symbol.
Line 3, first term: the image reads Q'' (d³z / dy² dt), as transcribed. The second term reads R'' (d⁴z / dx dy² dt); the print is faint but consistent with the transcription.
